correctness.rationale: The range of u=z−conjugate(w) is exactly Im u>0. In the Laplace integral the ordinary derivative multipliers are 1+iat−bt² and its conjugate, yielding density t[(1−bt²)²+a²t²]. Independent exact integration term by term gives −[u⁴+(12b−6a²)u²+120b²]/(πu⁶). A real polynomial avoids the open upper half-plane exactly when all its roots are real. For b≠0 the quadratic in u² has positive product, and a nonnegative discriminant implies a positive sum because b≤c_+a² and c_+<1/2. The discriminant is 12(3a⁴−12a²b−28b²); it is nonnegative exactly on the stated region. Outside it the two conjugate nonreal square levels give four distinct nonreal roots, two accessible. At a nontrivial boundary the numerator is a square of a real quadratic with two distinct real roots. The b=0 case has no accessible zeros, including the origin; the a=0,b≠0 case has strictly negative discriminant.
residual_risks: The real coefficients, ordinary-derivative normalization and unweighted half-plane assumptions are essential to this audit. The count is of scalar levels, not pairs.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The general ℓ¹ representation produces the numerator but does not itself classify mixed-jet zeros. The power-weight criterion includes the unweighted boundary at α=0; it is later dated and does not settle priority. Independently of this broader comparison, the separate unweighted entry directly covers the frozen claim.

evidence: The catalogue proof gives exactly two simple attainable roots in its lower-half-plane reciprocal variable away from the closed region, and two double real, unattainable roots on its nontrivial boundary. Every admissible reciprocal coordinate is attained. These details are not supplied by the cited general Gram representation alone.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Under the two invertible changes of variables the closed coefficient region, boundary, degeneracy at a=0 and off-cone accessible scalar count are the same theorem. Nothing in the frozen result remains after removing that covered content.

evidence: The indexed functional is f+af′+(B/2)f″ and its zero-free condition is a²≥B+sqrt(10/3)|B|. The indexed coordinate is t=1/(z−conjugate(w)).
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Set B=2b. Splitting the displayed bound at b=0 gives exactly the two frozen endpoints multiplying a² (and b=0 if a=0). The reciprocal maps the open upper half-plane onto the open lower half-plane and preserves multiplicities at nonzero roots.
